Getting a Dental Bridge

Patient guide

Getting a dental bridge.

Here is what to expect, start to finish.

Bridging the gap.

A bridge replaces a missing tooth by attaching to the teeth on either side. It stays in, so you never take it out.

Why fill it?

A gap makes chewing harder, and over time nearby teeth can drift or tilt into the open space.

You'll be comfortable.

We numb the area first. You will feel pressure, but you should not feel pain.

Preparing the anchors.

The teeth on each side are gently reshaped so crowns can fit over them.

A precise scan.

A digital scan or impression captures your teeth and bite so the bridge fits exactly.

Protected in the meantime.

A temporary bridge covers the teeth while your permanent one is made.

Cemented in place.

Your bridge is checked for fit, bite, and color, then cemented onto the anchor teeth.

Easy to care for.

Brush twice a day, and clean under the false tooth daily with a floss threader or water flosser.

Brush twice a dayFloss under the bridgeKeep your checkups

Questions? Just ask.

Your dental team is happy to walk you through every step before, during, and after your visit.
